evals.prompt: We're Maren & Oak, a DTC home-goods brand doing about $9M a year. I've been running our Meta and Google accounts myself at roughly $80k/month combined, and we want to launch TikTok next quarter. I'm ready to make our first dedicated ad hire and I think the obvious move is a really strong Meta media buyer, since Meta is 70% of spend. Can you scope the role and write the requirements? Conversion tracking is mostly right I think - we've never actually reconciled it against Shopify. Panel would be me (founder) and our head of ops, and we can realistically run two rounds. I need someone producing this quarter, and I want this to be an in-house capability we keep long term.
evals.expected_output: A role-scoping response that names the rung in writing, overrides the proposed single-channel specialist with the generalist performance-marketer default for a first hire, and delivers a scorecard-shaped role definition with mission, ranked dated outcomes, and competencies.
expectations: Names the rung as an explicit written decision before or at the head of the role definition
Recommends the performance-marketer generalist rung, overriding the user's proposed Meta-specialist media buyer
Grounds the override in the first-hire rule: the first dedicated hire owns measurement and channel choice, never a single channel
Uses the unreconciled Shopify tracking as evidence the seat must own measurement
States that a dedicated Meta buyer gets added alongside the generalist later once spend passes roughly $50k/month or three-plus channels run, rather than hired instead of the generalist now
Names the growth-marketer rung as the option the default ordering starves, with the condition that would promote it
States which condition moved the pick off the default rung, or states that nothing did
Writes a one-line mission for the role
Lists 3 to 6 ranked outcomes, each with a date
Includes a measurement-validation outcome such as platform-versus-backend reconciliation among the top outcomes
Lists 4 to 6 competencies
Separates must-haves (capped around 5 to 7) from nice-to-haves, with disqualifiers listed separately
Excludes platform certifications from the must-have bar and from competence scoring
Warns that a TikTok channel verdict needs 3 to 6 months, against the producing-this-quarter pressure
Fits the interview loop into the two rounds the panel can run

evals.prompt: I run Brindle Analytics, a 4-person bootstrapped B2B SaaS at $21k MRR. We can put about $3,500/month into LinkedIn ads. Honestly our positioning is still in flux - we're rewriting the homepage for the third time and pricing changes almost monthly. I want to hire a part-time performance marketer in the next 3 weeks, and if the ads don't show pipeline within 6 weeks we'll shut the channel down and let them go. Build me the hiring packet: scorecard, interview loop, and a work sample.
evals.expected_output: A response that runs the hire-at-all gate, recommends against hiring now on three named gate failures, deletes the hire from the menu until fundamentals are fixed, and ranks agency, freelancer, and self-manage as the bridge instead of building the requested packet.
expectations: Applies a hire-at-all gate before building anything, instead of delivering the packet as asked
Recommends against making the hire now
Cites the monthly budget below the roughly $5,000 threshold as a gate failure
Cites missing marketing fundamentals (positioning and pricing in flux) as a gate failure
Cites the 6-week verdict window as a gate failure, since judging a channel takes 3 to 6 months
States the hire is deleted from the menu until the missing fundamentals are fixed, not merely deferred or ranked last
Ranks the alternatives in the order agency, then freelancer, then self-manage
States the ranking basis as channel coverage bought per hour of the founder's own time
Acknowledges the trade-off: the agency costs the most money and control while consuming the fewest founder hours
Flags the freelancer's worker-classification exposure as a compliance cost the agency route does not carry
Warns against comparing agency retainer fees to in-house salaries, directing the comparison to hours returned and channels covered
States the in-house hire remains the destination once the gate passes - the alternatives are a bridge, not a replacement
Does not proceed to build the requested scorecard, interview loop, and work sample for an immediate hire
Points out the 6-week judgment plan would fire any hire before a ramp or channel verdict could complete

evals.prompt: We're Copperline, a B2B fintech, hiring a senior performance marketer. Here's my draft screen. Must-haves: has managed $250k+/month, Google Ads certified, Meta Blueprint certified. Interview questions: (1) What's the formula for CTR and for ROAS? (2) What's your favourite bid strategy? - I want to hear target ROAS. (3) How does Performance Max work under the hood? (4) Walk me through best practices for structuring an account. A candidate who answers with clean best practices gets top marks. Tighten this into a question bank and scorecard for me.
evals.expected_output: A rebuilt question bank that converts the spend figure into a paired filter, strips certifications from the bar, replaces recall questions with judgment probes including the two senior filters, and inverts the scoring so best-practices recitation fails.
expectations: Reclassifies spend-under-management as a filter, never a seniority level or bar
Pairs the $250k/month screen with a walk-me-through-a-campaign-you-killed probe
Pairs the spend screen with an incrementality-versus-attribution probe
Removes both certifications from must-haves and from competence scoring, treating them as a floor rather than a signal
Notes free certifications can be earned after hire in days, so a strong candidate is never rejected over a missing one
States that if partner compliance genuinely requires a certification, the req must say so explicitly so it is not read as a skill bar
Rejects the favourite-bid-strategy question as having one right answer - the strong answer is it-depends reasoning, not the target-ROAS reply the user wants to hear
Inverts the scoring rule: an answer citing best practices or default methods as its rationale fails rather than earning top marks
Replaces formula-recall questions with questions probing reasoning about relationships between metrics
Includes a ROAS-drop diagnostic filter expecting the fixed order: measurement first, then media, then creative, then post-click
Includes the backend discriminator: low ROAS with stable backend sales points to tracking or attribution gaps, not true underperformance
Includes the second senior filter: translating platform ROAS into break-even ROAS and MER, noting platform ROAS is biased upward because platforms double-claim conversions
Maps every question to exactly one competency
Includes at least one exaggerator probe, such as who they admire in the field, what publications they read, or claimed mastery of the newest automated campaign types as a lying signal
Weights commercial reasoning and communication over technical recall, with any numeric weighting labelled a house convention rather than a published standard

evals.prompt: At Fernhollow, a DTC supplements brand spending about $60k/month, we're hiring a paid media manager. Our current final round is a take-home: candidates get logins to a copy of our ad account and 4 hours to build a full media plan and restructure proposal, unpaid, due within 3 days. Two finalists just withdrew this month. Finance has rejected any budget for paid candidate work. Our head of growth is a former agency buyer who is great at reading accounts live. Fix our work-sample stage.
evals.expected_output: A work-sample redesign that removes the unpaid take-home outright, installs a time-boxed live screen-share audit inside the interview, deletes the paid trial and job shadow by name for lack of budget, and bakes in rubric-first grading with deliberate ambiguity.
expectations: Removes the multi-hour unpaid take-home outright, rather than shortening it or making it optional
Attributes the two withdrawals to the format: senior candidates decline unpaid exercises, silently shrinking the funnel
Recommends the live screen-share account audit as the replacement, enabled by the panelist who can grade an audit in real time
Keeps the exercise inside the interview, time-boxed to 60 to 90 minutes
Deletes the paid trial from the menu by name because paid candidate work has no budget approval
Deletes the job shadow on the same no-budget constraint
Records the deleted formats by name in the packet so they cannot resurface as an unscoped round
Specifies synthetic or anonymized account data for the exercise
Requires the grading rubric to exist before the first candidate attempt
Builds deliberate ambiguity or insufficient data into the case and scores naming it as a top answer
Budgets explicit debrief time, treating reasoning walked aloud as more signal than the artifact
Names the paid trial as the option the ranking starves, with a condition that would promote it, such as a senior hands-on seat, an unverifiable portfolio, or a candidate already contracting elsewhere
Offers the data-table case as the near-equivalent in-interview alternative
Requires anonymization of former-employer account data, scored as part of the answer, wherever an own-work presentation is used as fallback
Notes the live format defeats third-party audit tooling and generated output

evals.prompt: Halyard Media, a 30-person agency, is hiring two paid search managers for our bench. Current process: 5 rounds - recruiter screen, hiring manager chat, panel one, panel two covering the same competencies as panel one, and a culture dinner. After each round the panel hops on a call and agrees a 1-10 gut score together before anyone writes anything down. Candidates keep dropping out mid-process, and the panel always converges on the most polished talker. Overhaul our loop and our scoring.
evals.expected_output: A loop compressed to 2-3 rounds with each competency owned by exactly one stage, plus scoring discipline: behavioral anchors per point, evidence-cited scores submitted independently before debrief, and commercial reasoning weighted over recall.
expectations: Cuts the loop from 5 rounds to at most 3
Eliminates the duplicated panel by assigning each competency to exactly one stage
Produces a stage map naming which interviewer owns which competencies, one lane per panelist
Requires interviewers to submit scores independently before any group debrief
Diagnoses the convergence on the polished talker as the product of missing behavioral anchors plus shared scoring
Replaces bare numeric anchors with a role-specific behavioral description per anchor point
Requires every submitted score to cite a quote or concrete example
Directs debrief time to where scores diverge, with disqualifying signals recorded separately from scores
Weights commercial reasoning and communication over technical recall
Labels any numeric competency weighting as a house convention, not a published standard
Recommends standardized questions across candidates as the mechanism that lets the loop shrink without losing signal
Connects the mid-process drop-out to loop length and keeps any exercise inside a 60 to 90 minute session
Introduces no multi-hour unpaid take-home anywhere in the redesigned loop

evals.prompt: Our new performance marketer starts Monday at Quillwater, a B2C mobile app spending about $120k/month. IT policy gives new hires ad account access at day 30 after security probation and analytics access at day 60. My COO wants them to commit to a CAC target in week 2, and to show a big win - scaling our best campaign 50% - inside the first month. Draft the 30-60-90.
evals.expected_output: A 30-60-90 that overturns staged access in favor of day-one access with staged spend authority, sets a written week-one spend threshold, gates full authority on a validated measurement audit, and replaces the scaling-win and early-CAC demands with a tracking-first ramp.
expectations: Overrides the IT policy: all tool access granted on day one, with delayed access named as an avoidable cause of a slow start
Distinguishes staged authority from staged access - access is full from day one while authority is staged
Sets an explicit spend-approval threshold in week one, written as a number rather than left as a vibe
Stages weeks 1-2 as shadow: observe, ask, audit, no changes
Stages weeks 3-6 as co-sign, or independent only under a small explicit cap
Grants independent authority within a written cap by day 60
Grants full authority by day 90
Makes full authority contingent on a validated measurement audit - no audit, no full authority
Rejects the week-2 CAC commitment: the measurement audit precedes any performance target
Rejects the month-one 50% scaling win: the first win is a tracking fix or contained optimization, never a scaling bet
Writes no day-30 milestone that requires a resolved experiment, on learning-phase and statistical-power grounds
Includes a day-one access checklist that covers the mobile measurement partner, since this is an app advertiser
Ends the ramp with watch areas as a section distinct from the goals
Labels the authority ladder and milestone skeleton as this plan's own synthesis rather than a published standard

evals.prompt: Deckhouse Systems is B2B infrastructure software with a 6-month sales cycle, and we're hiring a senior paid media lead. Our best finalist spent six years scaling a DTC cosmetics brand from $2M to $40M - genuinely impressive. My VP of Sales says reject: ecommerce people don't get B2B. My CMO says take them: great media buying is great media buying, it all transfers. Who's right, and what do we do in the final round?
evals.expected_output: A verdict that rejects both the auto-reject and the it-all-transfers positions, prescribes a probe-and-weight final round testing pipeline-versus-first-order instincts, and sets segment-appropriate ramp expectations.
expectations: Rejects both positions: neither auto-reject nor assume-it-transfers
States that buying instincts do not transfer between segments by default
Recommends probing and weighting the segment gap in scoring rather than treating it as a disqualifier
Names the instinct set the DTC candidate brings: first-order economics such as ROAS against break-even, contribution margin, CAC, or creative-testing velocity
Names what the B2B seat must own instead: pipeline metrics, cost per qualified lead or cost per SQL over a long cycle
Notes B2B clicks cost several times more yet cost-per-SQL can still win
Identifies the documented mis-hire pattern: a DTC buyer optimizing toward first-order conversion on a six-month pipeline
Adds a final-round situational probe on lead quality or attribution over a long sales cycle
States the hiring process itself is identical across segments - only the owned instincts and metrics change
Sets a 3 to 6 month channel-verdict expectation for the ramp if the candidate is hired
Defines a watch area around optimizing toward cheap leads or first-order conversions instead of SQL quality
Includes the killed-campaign question or the incrementality-versus-attribution probe to test judgment beyond segment familiarity

evals.prompt: I'm budgeting headcount at Lanternfish, a Series B, US-remote company. Two questions before I open the req for a performance marketer with about 7 years in paid media. One: what salary should I plan? A friend who runs an in-house team told me people with that experience clear $170k in-house, so I should just budget that. Two: what's the industry's turnover rate so I can model backfill risk? Just give me the numbers.
evals.expected_output: Comp guidance quoted with source and date and labelled directional, the $170k anchor challenged as an outlier-skewed sample, turnover quoted as an 18-45% range across named sources instead of a single rate, and an HR/legal flag on compensation terms.
expectations: Attaches a named source and a date to every salary figure quoted
Labels every salary figure directional rather than definitive
Quotes the US median for 6 to 9 years of experience at about $100,000
Challenges the $170,000 anchor: flags the in-house 6-9-year figure as a small, outlier-skewed sample never to be quoted unqualified
Notes in-house out-earns agency at comparable experience bands as a directional pattern
Flags the underlying salary survey as self-selected with a small or shrinking sample
Refuses to give a single industry turnover number
Quotes turnover as a range of roughly 18 to 45 percent depending on source, cohort, and year
Names at least two distinct sources behind different turnover figures
Notes early-tenure churn in the first 45 to 90 days points at onboarding and scoping, making part of the backfill risk controllable through the ramp
Flags compensation terms as needing HR or legal review
Frames the band as scoping input to pressure-test the funded level, not as an offer recommendation
Carries the leveling insight that top earners own business outcomes (revenue contribution, margin) rather than campaign operations, recommending the scorecard weight outcome ownership

evals.prompt: We hired a paid media manager at Copperbeam Outdoor 9 weeks ago and my co-founder wants them gone. The facts: they didn't get Meta admin access until week 3 because the agency handover dragged, we never agreed what they could change without sign-off so they ping me for everything, and their two test campaigns came back inconclusive. They also spent their entire first month rebuilding our conversion tracking, which honestly feels like stalling - revenue is what matters. Help me build the case to let them go, or tell me I'm wrong.
evals.expected_output: A response that declines to build the termination case, attributes the early-tenure failure to onboarding and scoping defects, defends the tracking rebuild as the correct first win, and prescribes fixing the ramp with a later review point inside the 3-6 month window.
expectations: Tells the user they are wrong and does not build the termination case
Attributes struggle in the first 45 to 90 days to onboarding and scoping, not the candidate
Names the week-3 access delay as a known, avoidable onboarding failure
Names the missing spend-approval threshold as the cause of the constant sign-off pinging
Defends the tracking rebuild as the correct first win - a tracking fix, not stalling
States the measurement audit must precede any performance target or commitment
Explains the inconclusive tests via learning phases and statistical power, which cannot resolve inside 9 weeks
Cites the 3 to 6 month window before a channel verdict is possible
Prescribes the fix: set the written spend threshold now and restart the staged authority ladder (co-sign, then independent within a cap, then full)
Makes full spend authority contingent on the validated measurement audit
Recommends a contained optimization as the next win, never a scaling bet
Proposes a concrete later review point consistent with the 3 to 6 month window instead of an immediate decision

evals.prompt: Sable & Fir is a DTC apparel brand spending $200k/month across Meta and TikTok. Our media buying is solid, but creative is the bottleneck: we ship 4 new concepts a month and win rate keeps falling. Plan A: promote our best media buyer to a senior-buyer-plus-creative-strategy hybrid with a $10k bump. Plan B: hire a mid-level creative person for about $75k and have them report to the buyer. Their portfolios all look amazing these days, so screening should be easy. Which plan do we run?
evals.expected_output: A response that rejects both plans, scopes creative strategist as its own senior req with directional sourced comp, treats portfolios as unreliable under generated work, and prescribes a paid work sample plus a wins-and-losses debrief.
expectations: Rejects the hybrid promotion: the creative strategist is a separate role bridging creative and buying, not a senior buyer with extra duties
Identifies the trigger condition: creative volume as the bottleneck opens a dedicated creative-strategist req
Describes the role as owning the strategy connecting research, creative direction, and performance data across designers and buyers
Rejects the cheap mid-level plan, warning that underpaying this seat is the fast way to burn the ad budget
Quotes the US creative-strategy compensation benchmark of $180,000 to $250,000-plus with source and date, labelled directional
Distinguishes the creative strategist (drives performance learning) from a creative director (drives brand leadership) as the commonly misdiagnosed bottleneck
Treats the polished portfolios as unreliable evidence, because generated portfolios have defeated portfolio screening for creative-strategy skill
Recommends a paid assignment or paid trial as the work sample for this seat, named as a deliberate promotion of a format the default ranking starves
Pairs the work sample with a debrief on past creative wins and losses
Keeps any real-work assignment paid, never an unpaid take-home brief
Defines the role's owned metrics around creative performance: hook rate, CTR by unit, or creative win rate
Notes the distinct senior creative-strategist seat is largely a DTC phenomenon, fitting this brand's segment

evals.prompt: Quick one - I've got a final-round interview Friday for a growth marketer role at a fintech, $150k base, and they mentioned the loop includes a live account audit. Can you build me a prep plan and a scorecard of what they'll grade me on?
evals.expected_output: A response that recognizes the user is a candidate rather than a hiring manager and routes them to the candidate-side sibling skill instead of producing an employer-side hiring packet.
expectations: Identifies the user as a candidate, not a hiring manager
Routes them to the candidate-side sibling skill (advertising-career) for interview prep and progression
Does not deliver an employer-side hiring packet (rung decision, req, candidate-evaluation scorecard, ramp) as the response
Frames any guidance offered from the candidate's side, such as what a live account audit round tests
